messages.subject: Questions  about Missing Y Data
parts:
I'm working with a dataset where approximately 39% of the "sites" are associated with only 2 detections. Obviously it would be nice if only a few sites had only 2 or more surveys, but this is the data I am working with. I'm running a basic single-season model with covariates on occupancy and detection using jagSUI. 

My questions are: 

Should I drop the remaining surveys for sites with >2 if the model does not run smoothly?

Also: I've tried running the model with all of the data, but I'm confronted with the following error "one node produced an error, Error in node y[1,1]. Node inconsistent with parents". I read on the forum that in order for these models to work, the user should first supply JAGs with a value for Z (which I did) when establishing initial values. However, I'm still getting an error. Any thoughts on this? 

Here is the code; data is attached below.  Thanks.

#####Bayesian Hierarchical Models using JAGS (Single-Season Occupany Models)
##MUST DOWNLOAD JAGS for this to work!
#Model Set for All Rivers
data<-read.csv("pd_occu.csv", header = T, row.names = "ID")

#detection data; rows are sites columns are detection replicates
y<-data[,2:5]
n<-nrow(data)
n.occas<- ncol(y)

#Site Covariates
Period<- as.integer(data$Period)+1
DA<- log(data[,17])
PC1<- data[,13]
PC2<- data[,14]
Area<- log(data[,15])
Bar.Type<- log(data[,16])
Sinuosity<- log(data[,18])

##Drop Drainage Area & PC2, highly correlated
Covariates<- as.matrix(cbind(PC1, Area, Bar.Type, Sinuosity))

cor(Covariates)

#observation covariates
Effort<- data[,6:9]

#data for no-covariate model
jags.data<-list(y=y,n.sites=n,n.occas=n.occas)

##Simple Single-Season Occupancy Model, Constant Detection 
########################
require(jagsUI)
sink("occupancy.txt")
cat("
    model{
    #priors
    psi~dbeta(1,1)
    p~dbeta(1,1)
    for(i in 1:n.sites)
    {
    z[i]~dbern(psi)
    p.eff[i]<-z[i]*p
    for (j in 1:n.occas)
    {
    y[i,j]~dbern(p.eff[i])
    }
    
    }
    site.occup<-sum(z[])
    }
    ",fill=TRUE)
sink()



##vector to set initial occupancy state to 1 if 1 or more detection occurred at site.  speeds up BUGS, essential for JAGS
#JAGS can tempermental with initial values for params and NAs
z.init<-apply(jags.data$y,1,max)
initial<-function()list(p=runif(1,0,1),psi=runif(1,0,1),z=z.init)
params<-c("psi","p","site.occup")
inits<-list(initial(),initial(),initial())
occu_null <- jagsUI(data=jags.data, inits, parameters.to.save=params, model.file="occupancy.txt",n.thin = 5,n.chains = 3, n.burnin = 5000, n.iter =10000,parallel=TRUE)



Thanks,

Josh
